title: The Baba Yaga
summary: The ancient sorceress who ruled behind the Shadow Curtain.

claims.text: Before the tsars and the first tribal chiefs, the Baba Yaga was a sorceress, teacher and healer at one with Gaia, tending the land’s hurts.
In the early world a shadow fell over the sorceress and darkened that great mind, and the creatures and spirits that once listened now fled in terror.
In that despair the Wyrm offered, for a price, to make the wild obey once more; the Baba Yaga became its ally but never its mere pawn, with power close to an Incarna’s.
When the Baba Yaga rose and the Shadow Curtain fell in the early 1990s, supernatural Russia disappeared behind an invisible barrier.
In three nights the Baba Yaga’s forces purged almost every prominent vampire in Moscow, while the Garou saw little of the struggle.
In time it was unclear who was the prisoner behind the Curtain, the Garou or the Baba Yaga.
The Wyrm-dragon Grigori Deathwing, most loyal of the Zmei, woke to fight on the Baba Yaga’s side.

title: The death of the Baba Yaga

claims.text: Through 1998 the Garou dismantled the Baba Yaga’s power piece by piece, and that obsession with the werewolves may have left the sorceress open to vampire foes.
Many Black Spiral Dancers, disillusioned, quietly withdrew their aid, and other forces of the Wyrm came to see the sorceress as a liability.
The end came almost without climax, probably not at Garou hands; something older and darker had moved, and the Shadow Curtain died along with the Baba Yaga.
Some Garou leaders worry that an unknown destroyer is worse than a known foe, since the long-sleeping Baba Yaga never understood the modern world.

title: Septs of Russia
summary: Caerns that survived the Baba Yaga.

claims.text: A mysterious draining destroyed some Russian caerns and weakened others, and rumours tell of an artifact that might restore them.
The Sept of Gafnir’s Brood near St. Petersburg is a Get of Fenris Rage caern with a totem made of the furious ancestor spirits of Leningrad’s siege dead.
The Sept of the Kilakacn, an all-Glass Walker caern in a storage site of the Hermitage museum, has Cockroach as its totem.
Its oldest Garou, the lupus Ahroun Anton Nordenskald, the Grey Wolf of the Baltic, survived the war against the Baba Yaga as a keen strategist, as in the wars before it.

title: Black Tooth
summary: The deranged Simba king of Africa.

claims.text: Black Tooth, a Simba from Zululand, gathered a pride in the ivory wars of the late 1970s and struck at all European intruders, supernatural or mundane.
For fifteen years the Simba’s genocidal reign held the attention of all Africa’s shapeshifters, until a coalition of Bastet, Garou and Mokole broke the pride and scattered it.
That alliance has left African shapeshifters far less divided by hatred than those of Europe and the Americas.
Not all Ajaba were destroyed: some fled abroad, some fell to the Wyrm, and others hid with the Mokole by the Zambezi or with other Bastet.

title: The Amazon War and the Balam
summary: The struggle for South America’s rainforest.

claims.text: The battle for the South American rainforest is one of the great struggles of the Garou world.
The Amazon War strikes close to the Balam, the werejaguars, because their Kinfolk are among the native peoples of the region.
Solitary by nature, the Balam stay mostly in their dens in the Amazonian Umbra.
